title: January 2026 Protests: Morteza Yousefzadeh Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison
content:
HRANA – Morteza Yousefzadeh, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests who is currently incarcerated in Greater Tehran Prison, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison by the Tehran Revolutionary Court.

According to HRANA, Morteza Yousefzadeh has been sentenced to imprisonment.

Based on information received by HRANA, Branch 29 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Seyed Ali Mazloum, sentenced Mr. Yousefzadeh to 10 years in prison on charges including “taking operational action aimed at disrupting national security.”

Morteza Yousefzadeh was arrested in January 2026 amid nationwide protests. He has been held in Greater Tehran Prison since his arrest.

title: Three Baha’i Citizens Sentenced to 35 Years in Prison, Additional Punishments, and Property Confiscation
content:
According to HRANA, Baha’i citizens Hengameh Sharifinia, Fouad Abdolghaffari, and Fahim Agahi have been sentenced to prison and additional punishments.

The ruling was issued in late September by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Abolghasem Salavati. Under the ruling, Ms. Sharifinia was sentenced to 10 years in prison and 10 years of deprivation of social rights on the charge of “deviant educational or proselytizing activities contrary to or disruptive of the sacred law of Islam,” under Article 500 bis of the Islamic Penal Code. She was also sentenced to five years in prison on the charge of “membership in groups and organizations aimed at disrupting national security,” under Article 499 of the Islamic Penal Code.

title: Parviz Bangini Sentenced to Prison by Bukan Revolutionary Court
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, Parviz Bangini has been sentenced to prison.

According to the report, Branch of the Bukan Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Mehdi Fakhri, sentenced Mr. Bangini to eight months in prison on the charge of “propaganda against the regime.”

Parviz Bangini, a 29-year-old resident of Bukan, was arrested with the use of force by security forces at his residence on Wednesday, February 11, 2026. He was released after 35 days upon posting bail of one billion tomans. During his detention, he was also denied access to a lawyer, family visits, and phone calls with his family.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, Parviz Bangini has been sentenced to prison.

title: Mohammad Azizi Arrested and Transferred to Choobindar Prison in Qazvin
content:
According to information received by HRANA, Mohammad Azizi was arrested by IRGC Intelligence agents at his residence in Alvand on Wednesday, September 23. He was subsequently transferred to Choobindar Prison in Qazvin.

An informed source, confirming the news to HRANA, said that Mr. Azizi faces charges of “propaganda against the regime on the Internet,” “disrupting public order and peace,” “insulting the Supreme Leader,” and “insulting religious sanctities.”

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the specific acts cited as the basis for these charges.

Mohammad Azizi, a resident of Alvand, has previously faced arrest and judicial proceedings due to his activities.

title: Babak Roshan-Zamir Arrested and Transferred to Dehdasht Prison
content:
According to information received by HRANA, Mr. Roshan-Zamir was arrested by security forces in Likak on September 18, 2026, and was transferred to Dehdasht Prison approximately one week after his arrest.

An informed source close to his family told HRANA that he faces charges including “propaganda against the regime” and “collaboration with foreign networks.” Mr. Roshan-Zamir was reportedly arrested after visiting the graves of those killed during nationwide protests.

As of the time of this report, no further information has been obtained regarding the proceedings in his case or the conditions of his detention.

Babak Roshan-Zamir, a resident of Likak in Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad Province, has worked in the field of civil engineering.

title: Saravan: 9-Year-Old Child Dies After Military Forces Open Fire
content:
According to HRANA, citing Haal Vsh, a child has died after military forces opened fire.

He has been identified as Mohammad Amin Dehghan, 9, a resident of Jahadabad, Saravan.

According to the report, in the early hours of Thursday, September 24, Mohammad Amin and his father, Eshaq Dehghan, were traveling in a Saipa pickup truck carrying drinking water in the Jahadabad area of Shushtari (“Dab”), Saravan County, when their vehicle came under fire from military forces. Mohammad Amin sustained a severe gunshot wound to the head, while his father was also injured. Both were subsequently transported in another vehicle to Razi Hospital in Saravan.

After several days of hospitalization and medical treatment, Mohammad Amin Dehghan died on Sunday, September 27, due to the severity of his head injuries and the deterioration of his condition.

According to the outlet, at the time of the shooting, clashes were taking place in Jahadabad and the surrounding areas between military forces and armed individuals. However, no independent evidence has been published to date indicating that the vehicle carrying Mohammad Amin Dehghan and his father was connected to those clashes.

title: Six Teacher Union Activists Arrested Mamasani
content:
According to HRANA, citing the Coordinating Council of Iranian Teachers’ Trade Associations, the detainees have been identified as Shokrollah Ahmadi, Ali Safari, Ali Hassan Bahamin, Hojjat Sadat, Rasoul Bodaghi and Ghaffar Dindar.

According to the report, around noon on Friday, September 25, 2026, security forces arrived at a location in Mamasani County where the teachers’ union activists had gathered to visit a colleague and arrested them. Following interrogation, the detainees were transferred to Nurabad Prison in Mamasani on Saturday, September 26, 2026.

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrests or the charges brought against these union activists.

Shokrollah Ahmadi had previously been sentenced by a court to three years, seven months, and 15 days in prison. In January of 2026, he was arrested in connection with nationwide protests in Mamasani and was later released on bail. This teachers’ union activist has also previously faced judicial action because of his activities.

title: January 2026 Protests: Mahboubeh Shabani Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Mahboubeh Shabani has been sentenced to death.

According to information received by HRANA, Branch 1 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court sentenced Mahboubeh Shabani to death on the charge of “taking operational action to strengthen Israel, the United States, and individuals affiliated with opposition groups.”

The sentence was communicated on Saturday to the attorney representing Shabani, who remains incarcerated in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

The court hearing addressing the charges against Ms. Shabani was held on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, before the aforementioned judicial branch.

Mahboubeh Shabani was arrested by security forces in Mashhad on February 2, 2026, in connection with the nationwide protests and was subsequently transferred to Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

title: Zartosht Ahmadi Ragheb Sentenced to Prison in a New Case Filed Against Him While Incarcerated
content:
According to HRANA, Zartosht Ahmadi Ragheb has been sentenced to imprisonment and additional punishments.

According to information received by HRANA, in a new case opened against Mr. Ahmadi Ragheb during his imprisonment, a branch of the Karaj Revolutionary Court sentenced him to one year in prison. As additional punishments, he was also sentenced to a two-year travel ban and a two-year suspension from government and public services.

Information received by HRANA indicates that Zartosht Ahmadi Ragheb continues to be held alongside Masoud Farhikhteh in a separate room adjacent to Ward 16 that lacks basic facilities.

On August 19, 2026, a court hearing addressing the charges against Zartosht Ahmadi Ragheb was held via videoconference before a branch of the Karaj Revolutionary Court. During the hearing, Mr. Ahmadi Ragheb defended himself against charges including insulting the Supreme Leader, disrupting public order, and propaganda against the regime through the dissemination of false information.

On November 15, 2025, Mr. Ahmadi Ragheb was transferred from Ghezel Hesar Prison to Karaj Central Penitentiary.
snippet: According to HRANA, Zartosht Ahmadi Ragheb has been sentenced to imprisonment and additional punishments.

title: Three Prisoners Executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison, Karaj
content:
According to HRANA, three prisoners were executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

HRANA has identified the prisoners, who were hanged today, Sunday, September 27, 2026, as Hossein Jafari, Milad Zeinali, and Abbas Naghi. The latter two were residents of Kuhdasht.

According to information received by HRANA, Milad Zeinali was arrested eight years ago on drug-related charges and was subsequently sentenced to death by a Revolutionary Court. The other two prisoners were also arrested on similar charges and sentenced to death.

As of the time of this report, the executions of these prisoners have not been officially announced by prison officials or the relevant authorities.

According to HRA’s Annual Report, in 2025 at least 2,063 citizens, including 61 women and 2 juvenile offenders, were executed. Of these, the sentences of 11 individuals were carried out in public. During the same period, 172 other individuals were sentenced to death.
snippet: According to HRANA, three prisoners were executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.
